name: Costières de Nîmes

limits: For red and rosé wine, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah together: at least 60%
For red and rosé wine, Mourvèdre and Syrah together: at least 20%
For red and rosé wine, Marselan: at most 10%
For white wine, Grenache Blanc, Marsanne and Roussanne together: at least 50%
For white wine, Viognier: at most 20%

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

blurb.text: A Rhône Valley appellation between Nîmes and the western Rhône delta, in the Gard. Its wines resemble Rhône wines more than Languedoc ones. Reds and rosés are based on Grenache, Mourvèdre and Syrah, and whites on Grenache Blanc, Marsanne and Roussanne.
